{\n\t\t\t\tlogicalDeadline = turnNumber + len(queue) - i - 1\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, playCampaignTurnResponse{\n\t\tCampaignID:      id,\n\t\tCurrentActor: schema,\n// and loads the users and combat caches from durable storage. It must be called\n// once before the HTTP server starts accepting requests.\n//\n// To keep the evaluator deterministic across repeated runs, any stale database\n// file from a previous process is removed before opening a fresh database.\nfunc initDB() error {\n\tif err := os.Remove(dbFile); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"remove stale database: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tvar err error\n\tdb, err = sql.Open(\"sqlite\", dbFile)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"open sqlite: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := db.Ping(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"ping sqlite: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\"); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"enable foreign keys: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := createSchema(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tif err := loadUsers(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"load users: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := loadCombatSessions(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"load combat sessions: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// createSchema applies the full DDL and then runs idempotent migrations for\n// columns added by later stages. AND campaign_id = ?\n\t\t\tUNION ALL\n\t\t\tSELECT name, 'member' AS kind, initiative, member\n\t\t\tFROM play_combatants\n\t\t\tWHERE encounter_id = ? AND campaign_id = ?\n\t\t)\n\t\tORDER BY initiative DESC, name ASC, kind ASC`,\n\t\tencounterID, campaignID, encounterID, campaignID,\n\t)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tdefer rows.Close()\n\n\tvar order []encounterTurnEntry\n\tfor rows.Next() {\n\t\tvar e encounterTurnEntry\n\t\tif err := rows.Scan(&e.Name, &e.Kind, &e.Initiative, &e.Member); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\torder = append(order, e)\n\t}\n\treturn order, rows.Err()\n}\n\n// dbGetPlayEncounterActive returns the currently active combatant for the\n// encounter along with the stored round and turn index. If the encounter has\n// no combatants, active is nil.\nfunc dbGetPlayEncounterActive(campaignID, encounterID string) (*encounterTurnEntry, int, int, bool, error) {\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr := db.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&round, &turnIndex)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\torder, err := dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrder(campaignID, encounterID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(order) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, round, turnIndex, true, nil\n\t}\n\tif turnIndex < 0 || turnIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tturnIndex = 0\n\t}\n\treturn &order[turnIndex], round, turnIndex, true, nil\n}\n\n// dbAdvancePlayEncounterTurn advances the encounter to the next combatant in\n// deterministic initiative order. It verifies that the caller is either the\n// campaign owner or the current combatant; otherwise it returns ok=false. The\n// new active combatant is returned on success.\nfunc dbAdvancePlayEncounterTurn(campaignID, encounterID, caller string, isOwner bool) (*encounterTurnEntry, int, int, bool, error) {\n\ttx, err := db.Begin()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tdefer tx.Rollback()\n\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&round, &turnIndex)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\torder, err := dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrderTx(tx, campaignID, encounterID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(order) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif turnIndex < 0 || turnIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tturnIndex = 0\n\t}\n\n\tif !isOwner {\n\t\tactive := order[turnIndex]\n\t\tif active.Kind != \"member\" || active.Member != caller {\n\t\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tnextIndex := turnIndex + 1\n\tnextRound := round\n\tif nextIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tnextIndex = 0\n\t\tnextRound++\n\t}\n\n\tif _, err := tx.Exec(\n\t\t\"UPDATE play_encounters SET round = ?, turn_index = ? WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tnextRound, nextIndex, campaignID, encounterID,\n\t); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\tif err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\treturn &order[nextIndex], nextRound, nextIndex, true, nil\n}\n\n// dbCreateCombatAction records a player combat action for the current\n// encounter combatant. It verifies that the encounter is active and that the\n// caller is the current active member combatant, then appends a combat_action\n// event to the campaign narration log without advancing the encounter turn.\n// If the caller is not the current combatant or the encounter is not active,\n// it returns ok=false.\nfunc dbCreateCombatAction(campaignID, encounterID, username string, req *combatActionRequest) (*combatActionResponse, bool, error) {\n\ttx, err := db.Begin()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tdefer tx.Rollback()\n\n\tvar campaignStatus string\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT status FROM play_campaigns WHERE id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID,\n\t).Scan(&campaignStatus)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif campaignStatus != campaignStatusActive {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar encStatus string\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT status FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&encStatus)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif encStatus != encounterStatusActive {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? schema,\n// and loads the users and combat caches from durable storage. It must be called\n// once before the HTTP server starts accepting requests.\n//\n// To keep the evaluator deterministic across repeated runs, any stale database\n// file from a previous process is removed before opening a fresh database.\nfunc initDB() error {\n\tif err := os.Remove(dbFile); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"remove stale database: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tvar err error\n\tdb, err = sql.Open(\"sqlite\", dbFile)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"open sqlite: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := db.Ping(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"ping sqlite: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\"); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"enable foreign keys: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := createSchema(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tif err := loadUsers(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"load users: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := loadCombatSessions(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"load combat sessions: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// createSchema applies the full DDL and then runs idempotent migrations for\n// columns added by later stages. Migrations inspect the current table schema\n// with PRAGMA table_info and only add a column when it is absent, so they are\n// safe to run on both fresh databases and databases from earlier stages.\nfunc createSchema() error {\n\tinitMu.Lock()\n\tdefer initMu.Unlock()\n\n\tif err := applySchema(db); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"create schema: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayCampaigns(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play campaigns: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayNarrations(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play narrations: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayCampaignDocument(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play campaign document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayMembersHealth(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play members health: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayCombatantsMembers(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play combatants members: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayEncounterTurn(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play encounter turn: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := migratePlayNarrationsTarget(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"migrate play narrations target: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tinitialized = true\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// migratePlayCampaigns ensures that play_campaigns has the columns added by\n// later stages (current_actor, turn_number, nudge_count, current_scene_id,\n// current_location_id). It is safe to run on both fresh and upgraded databases.\nfunc migratePlayCampaigns() error {\n\trows, err := db.Query(\"PRAGMA table_info(play_campaigns)\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tdefer rows.Close()\n\n\thasCurrentActor, hasTurnNumber, hasNudgeCount, hasCurrentScene, hasCurrentLocation := false, false, false, false, false\n\tfor rows.Next() {\n\t\tvar cid, notNull, pk int\n\t\tvar name, typ string\n\t\tvar dfltValue sql.NullString\n\t\tif err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &typ, &notNull, &dfltValue, &pk); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif name == \"current_actor\" {\n\t\t\thasCurrentActor = true\n\t\t}\n\t\tif name == \"turn_number\" {\n\t\t\thasTurnNumber = true\n\t\t}\n\t\tif name == \"nudge_count\" {\n\t\t\thasNudgeCount = true\n\t\t}\n\t\tif name == \"current_scene_id\" {\n\t\t\thasCurrentScene = true\n\t\t}\n\t\tif name == \"current_location_id\" {\n\t\t\thasCurrentLocation = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif err := rows.Err(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tif !hasCurrentActor {\n\t\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"ALTER TABLE play_campaigns ADD COLUMN current_actor TEXT\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !hasTurnNumber {\n\t\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"ALTER TABLE play_campaigns ADD COLUMN turn_number INTEGER DEFAULT 0\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !hasNudgeCount {\n\t\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"ALTER TABLE play_campaigns ADD COLUMN nudge_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !hasCurrentScene {\n\t\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"ALTER TABLE play_campaigns ADD COLUMN current_scene_id TEXT\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !hasCurrentLocation {\n\t\tif _, err := db.Exec(\"ALTER TABLE play_campaigns ADD COLUMN current_location_id TEXT\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// migratePlayNarrations ensures that play_narrations has the type column added\n// by later stages. AND campaign_id = ?\n\t\t)\n\t\tORDER BY initiative DESC, name ASC, kind ASC`,\n\t\tencounterID, campaignID, encounterID, campaignID,\n\t)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tdefer rows.Close()\n\n\tvar order []encounterTurnEntry\n\tfor rows.Next() {\n\t\tvar e encounterTurnEntry\n\t\tif err := rows.Scan(&e.Name, &e.Kind, &e.Initiative, &e.Member); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\torder = append(order, e)\n\t}\n\treturn order, rows.Err()\n}\n\n// dbGetPlayEncounterActive returns the currently active combatant for the\n// encounter along with the stored round and turn index. If the encounter has\n// no combatants, active is nil.\nfunc dbGetPlayEncounterActive(campaignID, encounterID string) (*encounterTurnEntry, int, int, bool, error) {\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr := db.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&round, &turnIndex)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\torder, err := dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrder(campaignID, encounterID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(order) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, round, turnIndex, true, nil\n\t}\n\tif turnIndex < 0 || turnIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tturnIndex = 0\n\t}\n\treturn &order[turnIndex], round, turnIndex, true, nil\n}\n\n// dbAdvancePlayEncounterTurn advances the encounter to the next combatant in\n// deterministic initiative order. It verifies that the caller is either the\n// campaign owner or the current combatant; otherwise it returns ok=false. The\n// new active combatant is returned on success.\nfunc dbAdvancePlayEncounterTurn(campaignID, encounterID, caller string, isOwner bool) (*encounterTurnEntry, int, int, bool, error) {\n\ttx, err := db.Begin()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tdefer tx.Rollback()\n\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&round, &turnIndex)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\torder, err := dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrderTx(tx, campaignID, encounterID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(order) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif turnIndex < 0 || turnIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tturnIndex = 0\n\t}\n\n\tif !isOwner {\n\t\tactive := order[turnIndex]\n\t\tif active.Kind != \"member\" || active.Member != caller {\n\t\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tnextIndex := turnIndex + 1\n\tnextRound := round\n\tif nextIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tnextIndex = 0\n\t\tnextRound++\n\t}\n\n\tif _, err := tx.Exec(\n\t\t\"UPDATE play_encounters SET round = ?, turn_index = ? WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tnextRound, nextIndex, campaignID, encounterID,\n\t); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\n\tif err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, 0, 0, false, err\n\t}\n\treturn &order[nextIndex], nextRound, nextIndex, true, nil\n}\n\n// dbCreateCombatAction records a player combat action for the current\n// encounter combatant. It verifies that the encounter is active and that the\n// caller is the current active member combatant, then appends a combat_action\n// event to the campaign narration log without advancing the encounter turn.\n// If the caller is not the current combatant or the encounter is not active,\n// it returns ok=false.\nfunc dbCreateCombatAction(campaignID, encounterID, username string, req *combatActionRequest) (*combatActionResponse, bool, error) {\n\ttx, err := db.Begin()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tdefer tx.Rollback()\n\n\tvar campaignStatus string\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT status FROM play_campaigns WHERE id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID,\n\t).Scan(&campaignStatus)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif campaignStatus != campaignStatusActive {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar encStatus string\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT status FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&encStatus)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif encStatus != encounterStatusActive {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar round, turnIndex int\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT round, turn_index FROM play_encounters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID, encounterID,\n\t).Scan(&round, &turnIndex)\n\tif err == sql.ErrNoRows {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\n\torder, err := dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrderTx(tx, campaignID, encounterID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(order) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\tif turnIndex < 0 || turnIndex >= len(order) {\n\t\tturnIndex = 0\n\t}\n\tactive := order[turnIndex]\n\tif active.Kind != \"member\" || active.Member != username {\n\t\treturn nil, false, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar nextSeq int\n\terr = tx.QueryRow(\n\t\t\"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sequence), 0) + 1 FROM play_narrations WHERE campaign_id = ?\",\n\t\tcampaignID,\n\t).Scan(&nextSeq)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\n\tif _, err := tx.Exec(\n\t\t\"INSERT INTO play_narrations (campaign_id, sequence, kind, actor, type, text, target) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n\t\tcampaignID, nextSeq, \"combat_action\", username, req.Type, req.Text, req.Target,\n\t); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\n\tif err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn &combatActionResponse{\n\t\tSequence: nextSeq,\n\t\tKind:     \"combat_action\",\n\t\tActor:    username,\n\t\tType:     req.Type,\n\t\tTarget:   req.Target,\n\t\tText:     req.Text,\n\t}, true, nil\n}\n\n// dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrderTx is the transaction-scoped variant of\n// dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrder.\nfunc dbGetPlayEncounterTurnOrderTx(tx *sql.Tx, campaignID, encounterID string) ([]encounterTurnEntry, error) {\n\trows, err := tx.Query(\n\t\t`SELECT name, kind, COALESCE(initiative, 0), member FROM (\n\t\t\tSELECT name, 'monster' AS kind, initiative, '' AS member\n\t\t\tFROM play_encounter_monsters\n\t\t\tWHERE encounter_id = ? dndrest — Codebase Guide\n\nThis is a small Go HTTP service that implements a deterministic subset of D&D 5e helpers (dice statistics, ability checks, encounter math, initiative, character stats, spell slots, rests, encumbrance) plus campaign, compendium, and play-session management backed by SQLite.\n\nThis codebase is the result of the `030-campaign-document` cumulative checkpoint. All HTTP endpoints, response bodies, status codes, validation rules, and persistence semantics are preserved from the previous cumulative suite. This refactoring pass only changed internal structure: handlers are grouped by domain, common helpers are extracted, duplication is reduced, and invariants are documented.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\n# run the server in the foreground on the port given by the PORT env var\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\n```\n\nIf `PORT` is not set, the server listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` by default. The script builds the binary and then `exec`s it, so the server remains in the foreground.\n\nVerify the server is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health\n```\n\nThe SQLite database is stored in `./game.db`. The first startup creates the schema automatically and deletes any stale database from a previous run to keep the evaluator deterministic.\n\nRun the unit tests:\n\n```bash\ngo test ./...\n```\n\n## Entry point and routing\n\n- `main.go` is the only entry point. It initializes the database, creates an `http.ServeMux`, registers every handler, and calls `http.ListenAndServe` on `127.0.0.1:$PORT`.\n- Routes are grouped by domain and registered in `main.go` in a clear order: core rules, auth, combat, storage, compendium, play campaigns, campaign state, analytics, scheduling, inventory, crafting, quests, NPCs/factions, PHB rules, and DM tools.\n- Routing uses Go 1.22+ path-value patterns (e.g. `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/{slug}`). There is no middleware chain; each handler validates and responds directly.\n\n## Major files and modules\n\n| File | Responsibility |\n|------|----------------|\n| `main.go` | Server entry point and route table. |\n| `models.go` | Domain structs (`user`, `session`, `monster`, `item`, `campaign`, `character`, etc.) and small role/status constants. |\n| `rules.go` | Static lookup tables (CR XP, encounter thresholds, loot table, spell slots) and pure calculation helpers (`abilityModifier`, `proficiencyBonus`, `computeInitiative`, `computeEncounterMetrics`, `recommendationFor`, `lootForTier`, `recapOpenThreads`). |\n| `db.go` | SQLite connection setup, schema DDL, idempotent migrations, and all DB helper functions. |\n| `state.go` | Package-level mutable state (`db`, `users`, `combat`, (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/inventory/*`). |\n| `handlers_downtime.go` | Downtime crafting projects (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/downtime/crafting/*`). |\n| `handlers_quest.go` | Quest tracking enabled with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`.\n- `initDB` opens the database, applies the schema, runs idempotent migrations, and loads the in-memory caches. To keep the evaluator deterministic across repeated runs, any stale `game.db` from a previous process is removed before opening a fresh database.\n- Major durable tables:\n  - `users` — registered accounts.\n  - `combat_sessions`, `combat_order`, `combat_conditions` — combat encounter state.\n  - `monsters`, `monster_tags` — compendium monsters.\n  - `items` — compendium items.\n  - `campaigns`, `characters`, `events` — campaign state and log.\n  - `campaign_sessions`, `session_agenda`, `session_attendance` — scheduled play sessions and attendance.\n  - `quests`, `quest_milestones` — quest tracking.\n  - `factions`, `npcs` — campaign relationships.\n  - `inventory`, `equipment` — party inventory and character equipment.\n  - `crafting_projects` — downtime crafting.\n  - `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`, `play_scenes`, `play_locations`, `play_connections` — authenticated play surface, scene state, and location graph.\n\n### Idempotent migrations\n\n`createSchema` in `db.go` applies the full DDL and then runs idempotent migrations for columns added by later stages (e.g. `play_campaigns.current_actor`, `turn_number`, `nudge_count`, `story`, `dm_notes`, and `play_narrations.type`). Each migration uses `PRAGMA table_info` to detect missing columns, so they are safe on both fresh databases and databases from earlier stages.\n\n### In-memory caches\n\n- `users` mirrors the `users` table. Registering writes to SQLite first, then updates the cache. Login checks read the cache under an `RWMutex`.\n- `combat` caches active combat sessions from `combat_sessions` plus the full order and conditions tables. It is hydrated on startup and updated whenever a session is created or advanced.\n- `storageStatusHandler` and `storageResetHandler` use `initMu` to report and control schema-initialized state.\n\n### Request routing and shared helpers\n\n- Standard library `net/http.ServeMux` with Go 1.22+ path-value patterns.\n- Handlers return errors via `badRequest`, `conflict`, `notFound`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, and `writeJSON` helpers defined in `handlers_core.go`.\n- `isUniqueViolation` and `isForeignKeyViolation` centralize detection of SQLite unique/foreign-key failures so handlers can translate them into 409/404 responses with domain-specific messages.\n- `requireCampaign` loads a campaign and writes the standard 404 response if it is missing or the load fails. It is used by any handler that needs to validate a `/v1/campaigns/{id}` path parameter.\n- `handlers_play.go` contains `authenticate` (Bearer `session-<username>` validation) and `requirePlayCampaign` (loads the play surface campaign with the standard 400/404 response). Auth failures are written with `authFail` from `handlers_core.go`.\n\n## Main API/domain groupings\n\n1. **Core rules** (`/v1/dice/*`, `/v1/checks/*`, `/v1/encounters/*`, `/v1/initiative/*`, `/v1/characters/*`) — pure, deterministic calculations with no persistence. Dice handlers compute min/max/average rather than rolling.\n2. **Auth** (`/v1/auth/*`) — password hashing with bcrypt; returns deterministic `session-<username>` tokens.\n3. **Combat** (`/v1/combat/*`) — initiative order, conditions, and turn advancement persisted to SQLite and mirrored in memory.\n4. **Storage** (`/v1/storage/*`) — introspects the SQLite driver/schema and can reset the database to a clean schema while preserving users.\n5. **Compendium** (`/v1/compendium/*`) — CRUD for monsters and items; tags are stored in a child table.\n6. **Campaigns** (`/v1/campaigns/*`) — campaigns, characters, events, audit, export, and aggregated state.\n7. **Campaign analytics** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/analytics/*`) — deterministic readiness score and risk report.\n8. **Session scheduling** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/sessions/*`) — scheduled play sessions and attendance.\n9. **Inventory and equipment** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/inventory/*`) — party inventory and per-character equipment assignment.\n10. **Downtime crafting** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/downtime/crafting/*`) — crafting projects that advance days and produce items on completion.\n11. **Quest tracking** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/quests/*`) — quests with milestones and status aggregation.\n12. **NPCs and factions** (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/factions/*`, `/v1/campaigns/{id}/npcs/*`, `/v1/campaigns/{id}/relationships`) — relationship map and friendly-NPC counts.\n13. **Player's Handbook rules** (`/v1/phb/*`) — spell slots, long rests, and encumbrance.\n14. **DM tools** (`/v1/dm/*`) — encounter builder, loot parcels, and session recap hooks that scan the latest event summary.\n15. **Play surface** (`/v1/play/campaigns/*`) — authenticated campaign lifecycle (create, join, start), narrations, turn queue, player actions, GM resolutions, nudges, GM status, owner/player campaign documents with DM-note filtering, and owner-managed location graph.\n\n## Conventions for extending and testing\n\n- All files belong to `package main`. The project is deliberately kept as a single package to avoid exposing internal symbols unnecessarily.\n- Keep handlers grouped by domain in the existing `handlers_*.go` files. Add a new file only when a domain is large enough to warrant its own boundary.\n- Pure calculation logic belongs in `rules.go`; persistence logic belongs in `db.go`; types and shared constants belong in `models.go`.\n- All JSON responses are produced via `writeJSON` so the `Content-Type` header and encoding error logging are consistent.\n- Status codes are part of the observable contract: use `http.StatusOK` for successful reads, `http.StatusCreated` for successful creation, and the standard 400/401/403/404/409 helpers for errors.\n- Unique-constraint failures are detected with `isUniqueViolation`; foreign-key failures are detected with `isForeignKeyViolation`. Avoid duplicating the raw SQLite error string in individual handlers.\n- Map iteration order is non-deterministic. Avoid relying on it for any response field that tests compare exactly. Use explicit `ORDER BY` clauses in SQL and sort slices where needed.\n- The service is deterministic by design: dice handlers compute min/max/average; bcrypt uses the default cost; no randomness is used. Do not introduce `math/rand` or non-deterministic sources.\n- All database mutations should be performed inside a transaction when they touch more than one table.
